This justification authorizes and dictates the acquisition of specific, brand-name industrial automation, network, and scanning hardware—specifically Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories (SEL) network switches, Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley control platforms, and Datalogic industrial scanners—necessary to support the deployment, integration, and sustainment of the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Material Flow System (MFS). The requirement for these specific manufacturers is based entirely on the technical parameters of the existing solution and the DLA Enterprise Approved Architecture, not on subjective vendor preference. Standardizing on these chosen enterprise brands is operationally necessary to align long-term sustainment, configuration management, and maintenance processes. Utilizing non-standard hardware would introduce disparate system architectures, exponentially increasing lifecycle maintenance costs and degrading operational readiness by disrupting the required interoperability across the physical and digital layers of DLA's critical material-handling infrastructure. Additionally, alternative hardware options present unacceptable risks of containing components manufactured in prohibited foreign nations, specifically the People's Republic of China. Utilizing hardware with Chinese-origin components violates strict DoD supply chain security directives designed to prevent cyber-espionage and hardware-level vulnerabilities. Standardizing on this approved, vetted hardware stack guarantees supply chain integrity, minimizes geopolitical risk, and ensures immediate compliance with DoD information assurance mandates. Based on the facts stated above, brand-name Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories (SEL) network switches, Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley control platforms, and Datalogic industrial scanners are essential to the Government’s needs and market research indicates there are no other products on the market that can satisfy the immediate requirement. 5. We work in partnership with all agencies/bodies under the aegis of the Department – a comprehensive listing including all of the Boards/Tribunals under our aegis and their functions can be found on the Department's website https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-justice-home-affairs-and-migration/ About the Managed Service Contract and the Procurement Procedure The Irish Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) verifies electronic Residence Permits (eRP) conforming to European legislation (Council Regulation 2002/1030/EC, Council Regulation 2008/380/EC, Commission Decision C (2009)3770, Commission Decision C (2011)5478). The PKI infrastructure (comprising software and High Security Module (HSM)) decrypts information on a physical card and verifies the authenticity of the card containing the encrypted information. There were approximately 340,000 eRPs processed in 2024, and approximately 320,000 in 2025. ately 320,000 in 2025.
